name: Garage Museum
watch: Garage paused exhibitions in February 2022 and showed its collection again in 2024. Security services searched its offices in April 2024.
why_flagged: Non-profit project of the IRIS Foundation, founded by Roman Abramovich and Dasha Zhukova. Its endowment page lists Abramovich's gifts from 2018 to 2023; he is on UK and EU sanctions lists.
records_note: The Garage endowment fund posts reports and statutory audit results for 2019 to 2025 and a named donor list by year; two trustees are named.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2008-09: The same cable says Abramovich paid to build the Bakhmetevsky garage exhibition space, Garage's home from 2008, as a gift for Darya Zhukova. (Cablegate 08MOSCOW2700)

name: SONGEUN
watch: Founder's company is a coal miner and trader.
why_flagged: Founder's company is a coal miner and trader.
records_note: The foundation posts yearly donation disclosures for 2022 to 2025, with a 2024 audit report, but no annual report, donor list or board.

name: Guggenheim Bilbao
watch: Petronor refinery sits on the board.
why_flagged: Petronor refinery sits on the board.
records_note: It posts the 2025 activity report and 2025 accounts for three entities, and lists corporate members by name; trustees show only as organisations.

name: Kunsthaus Zürich
watch: Bührle arms fortune and Nazi-era provenance, in litigation.
why_flagged: Bührle arms fortune and Nazi-era provenance, in litigation.
records_note: Its 2024 annual report carries full accounts with an audit report and a logo image of funding partners, but names only the board chair.

name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
watch: Politically tinged defunding 2018; 2025 works removed under embassy pressure.
why_flagged: Politically tinged defunding 2018; 2025 works removed under embassy pressure.
records_note: Its site lists the foundation committee and named supporters, but it blocked page fetches, so annual reports and accounts could not be checked.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
watch: Kafala labour abuses documented by HRW.
why_flagged: Owned by the Abu Dhabi Department of Culture and Tourism. Abu Dhabi pays France €400M for the Louvre name and €190M for loans under the 2007 agreement.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2018 to 2023 and names partners and patrons; the site blocked fetches, so accounts and board could not be checked.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2008-01 to 2009-05: Cables tie the Louvre deal to France's naval base and nuclear bid in the UAE, all Mohammed bin Zayed initiatives. State-owned TDIC develops the museum. Sarkozy laid its first stone in 2009, the year Human Rights Watch reported worker abuse on Saadiyat. (Cablegate, 4 cables)

name: Sharjah Art Foundation
watch: Gulf state body; 2011 censorship and director's sacking.
why_flagged: Gulf state body; 2011 censorship and director's sacking.
records_note: Its site has no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board list; the sponsors page names no one.

name: Collective
watch: Dropped Baillie Gifford (£25k) in March 2024 under pressure.
why_flagged: Dropped Baillie Gifford (£25k) in March 2024 under pressure.
records_note: It posts no annual reports, files returns with the Scottish charity regulator, shows three funder logos with no names or date, and lists its trustees.

name: Edinburgh International Book Festival
records_note: It posts impact reports for 2024 and 2025, files accounts with the Scottish regulator, names funders and sponsors undated, and lists its trustees.

name: Stills
watch: Ended Baillie Gifford funding in June 2024.
why_flagged: Ended Baillie Gifford funding in June 2024.
records_note: It posts no annual reports, files accounts with the Scottish regulator, names 19 funders and supporters undated, and lists three board members.

name: Hay Festival
records_note: It posts no annual reports, files accounts at Companies House, names Airbnb and other partners without a date, and lists 12 trustees.

name: British Museum
watch: Trustee Ahdaf Soueif resigned over BP in 2019; 80 signed a 2023 open letter. The Sackler name left by agreement in 2022.
why_flagged: BP gives £50M over ten years for the masterplan, announced 19 December 2023. The Sackler name came off its rooms and endowments in 2022.
records_note: It posts reports and audited accounts for 2022 to 2025, names donors in its 2022-23 review, and lists 21 trustees on its governance page.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, c. 2011: The same item says Iran's National Museum cut ties with the British Museum in early 2010 over the delayed Cyrus Cylinder loan, and restored them once the cylinder went to Tehran. (Stratfor emails (Fars News item))
